title: Text Interpolation
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of Text Interpolation in a Vue 3 application.
Apply at least one of the syllabus subtopics in a small, inspectable example.
Verify one expected behavior and identify a relevant edge case.

content.intro: This lesson studies Text Interpolation within Vue Template Syntax. The source PDF subtopics are preserved below and connected to an original working-style example.
content.why_it_matters: Templates keep intent visible: the UI describes what should appear for the current state instead of manually editing the DOM.

content_blocks.title: Text Interpolation: Declarative template rendering
content_blocks.alt_text: Declarative template rendering diagram for lesson 15: Text Interpolation. Keep template expressions small and readable → Choose conditions, lists, attributes, or events → Use stable keys and predictable output
content_blocks.caption: Template flow: bind application state declaratively and select directives according to the desired DOM behavior.

content_blocks.title: The idea in context
content_blocks.text: Vue templates bind readable HTML-like markup to data and events, using expressions and directives for dynamic behavior. This lesson focuses on Text Interpolation. Start by naming the state, component, browser behavior, or deployment boundary involved; then predict what should change and test the smallest example.

items.title: Double-curly-brace syntax
items.text: For Double-curly-brace syntax, connect the term to a visible behavior in a small Vue 3 example. State what input or reactive dependency changes, predict the UI result, and verify the prediction with a normal case plus a boundary case.

items.title: Rendering strings and numbers
items.text: For Rendering strings and numbers, express the intended DOM result through a Vue template binding instead of directly manipulating the DOM. Keep template expressions small, use stable keys for stateful list items, and choose directives based on whether content should be created, removed, or merely hidden.

items.title: Evaluating simple expressions
items.text: For Evaluating simple expressions, express the intended DOM result through a Vue template binding instead of directly manipulating the DOM. Keep template expressions small, use stable keys for stateful list items, and choose directives based on whether content should be created, removed, or merely hidden.

content_blocks.expected_output: The paragraph shows “Hello, Ada.”; changing name updates the text without manual DOM edits.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Use as App.vue in a local Vue 3 project and change the initial name to inspect the reactive result.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the initial values or original code, reload the development app/test, and repeat once with a boundary or failure case. Remove temporary logs and test data before committing.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Work through Text Interpolation with a predict–change–verify loop. First state the expected UI or console output. Change only the relevant input/state value, then observe the result. Compare it with the expected output in the code block; if it differs, check the exact file, runtime/version, browser Console, and network response before widening the investigation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the example to include “Rendering strings and numbers”. Keep the same behavior for the ordinary input, then try an empty, invalid, repeated, or failure condition that makes sense for the example. Record the expected result before testing.

items.title: Assuming behavior instead of checking it
items.text: Write down the expected result and reproduce the issue in the smallest possible example; inspect the browser Console and the exact reactive value or request.

items.title: Ignoring an edge case
items.text: Try empty input, a missing item, repeated interaction, a failed request, or unmounting while work is pending; handle the case explicitly.

items.title: Putting every responsibility in one component
items.text: Separate display, reusable logic, API service, and shared state when that boundary makes the behavior easier to test and explain.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember: Vue templates bind readable HTML-like markup to data and events, using expressions and directives for dynamic behavior. For Text Interpolation, keep the example small, verify the rendered or logged result, and consult the official references when behavior depends on a specific Vue or ecosystem version.

content_blocks.title: Accessibility, version, and runtime notes
content_blocks.text: Use semantic HTML, readable labels, keyboard-operable controls, and visible errors where the example interacts with users. Vue examples are intended for Vue 3.x with create-vue/Vite unless a legacy or specialist lesson explicitly says otherwise. This CodeLeaf playground does not execute arbitrary Vue code; the snippets are labeled for static validation and should be run in a separate local project.

content.task: Create a small example for “Text Interpolation” that applies “Double-curly-brace syntax”, predicts the expected result, and verifies a relevant boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named Vue concept rather than only mentioning it.
The expected output or observable behavior is written down and can be checked locally.
At least one boundary, loading, invalid-input, or failure case is tested or explicitly reasoned about.
The example uses semantic/accessible interaction patterns and does not treat frontend state as authoritative security.
hints: Start with the smallest observable part of “Double-curly-brace syntax”.
Predict the output before changing one input at a time.
Use the browser Console, Vue DevTools, or the appropriate test runner to isolate a mismatch.

common_mistakes.problem: The example only covers the happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Real interfaces receive empty values, delayed responses, invalid input, and failed requests.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one realistic edge/failure case and state its expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: The code assumes an API or feature exists in every runtime.
common_mistakes.why: Tool and API support depends on Vue, the build tool, or the chosen SSR/test framework.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the linked official reference and record the runtime/version assumption.

summary: Text Interpolation belongs to the broader area Vue Template Syntax.
The main concept to practice is Double-curly-brace syntax.
Verify a normal result and one meaningful boundary case before using the pattern in a production feature.
